_comment: Machine-readable form of EVAL_QUESTIONS.md. The markdown is the document a human
reads and is the source of truth for intent; this file is what the harness runs.
Question text is copied verbatim, including the lowercase and the missing
apostrophes -- these are what an on-call engineer actually types at 2 AM, and
cleaning them up would make retrieval look better than it is.
expected_class is what SHOULD happen, from EVAL_QUESTIONS.md section 2.
expected_documents is what the answer needs, not everything that might be relevant.
service is the scope the detector would supply; null means no service scope,
which is itself part of the test for the vague and meta questions.

questions.text: checkout throwing 503s, where do i start?
questions.note: The baseline case. Two documents, ordered: classify with RB-PAY-000 first.

questions.text: refunds failing too — same payment-service problem or separate thing?
questions.note: Planted partial-answer test, run in the harder direction. Sibling corroboration lives only in RB-PAY-002; RB-PAY-001 does not even cross-reference it.

questions.text: only mobile-app getting errors, what do i check that's different from web?
questions.note: UNPLANNED GAP. Fragments exist; no consumer-dimension triage procedure. Must say so.

questions.text: payment-service just deployed, can i roll it back or do i need approval?
questions.note: The restricted document. Must be named as existing-but-unavailable, never as absent.

questions.text: a few login 401s — actual incident or people getting passwords wrong?
questions.note: RB-AUTH-000's answer is in its (overview) section -- the untitled preamble that section-iterating chunking would have dropped.

questions.text: search is really slow but all 200s, does that count as degraded?
questions.note: Capacity against fault, plus declared objectives.

questions.text: 3 refund failures and barely any traffic, enough to wake someone up?
questions.note: Strongest question in the set. Three documents. Two-sided answer: does not clear the floor, and that is not the same as nothing being wrong.

questions.text: timeouts stopped but latency still high, can i close this?
questions.note: UNPLANNED GAP. No closure criteria anywhere. POL-SEV-001 covers time-to-classification and says so explicitly.

questions.text: cart works but orders failing, which inventory-service checks apply?
questions.note: Negative-corroboration nuance: the two endpoints exercise different paths, so a quiet /cart is weak evidence.

questions.text: partner-api getting 429s, where are the limits documented?
questions.note: No rate-limit documentation. Corpus is 5xx and latency only.

questions.text: admin-portal blank but web-app fine, frontend issue or something behind it?
questions.note: No client-side or frontend guidance. CDN and edge are an explicit manifest 4.4 gap.

questions.text: two payment runbooks say different things, which one is current?
questions.note: THE STATUS-FILTER DEMO. RB-PAY-000-ARCHIVED must not be presented as current. Run both ways on video.

questions.text: payment restart procedure — what needs checking first?
questions.note: A strong refusal quotes the 'classification only, not remediation' scope line rather than just saying no.

questions.text: checkout timed out, is retrying safe or could we charge twice?
questions.note: Most interesting question in the set. Retry reasoning lives on a different endpoint on a different service. Correct answer is escalate; watch whether it cites across services and how it hedges.

questions.text: inventory owner not answering, who's next on escalation?
questions.note: PLANTED STALE ENTRY. CAT-DEP-001 says order-fulfilment, a superseded name. The best answer names the conflict rather than silently picking one.

questions.text: failures across unrelated endpoints, how do i check gateway vs dns?
questions.note: No gateway-level or DNS guidance.

questions.text: could the external payment provider be down, where do we check that?
questions.note: BEST REFUSAL IN THE SET -- the corpus refuses itself. CAT-DEP-001 states no downstream dependencies are declared, that this is not an assertion that none exist, and that such questions escalate. Should cite that passage, not go silent.

questions.text: alert firing but no recent logs, is the service quiet or is logging broken?
questions.note: Telemetry-pipeline health not covered. POL-SLO-001's bucket precondition is adjacent but does not answer it.

questions.text: refund says success but customer hasn't got the money, where do we trace it?
questions.note: Correctness rather than availability -- class 4, invisible in both series. No tracing procedure exists. Classify, escalate, do not reconstruct.

questions.text: everything looks bad, what do i check first?
questions.note: Genuinely too vague. Tests whether the system asks for narrowing or dumps every runbook it has.

questions.text: do we even have a runbook for this?
questions.note: META-QUESTION about coverage, not content. Correct behaviour is to report what exists rather than answer an unstated question.

questions.text: is this only one region? wait we only have one region — what's the fallback?
questions.note: FALSE PREMISE, self-corrected mid-sentence. Must follow the correction, then refuse -- nothing on regional fallback.

questions.text: payment declined but inventory still reserved
questions.note: Cross-service state inconsistency, two teams, no single runbook. RB-INV-000's divergence procedure is adjacent but covers cart-versus-order. Watch for over-transfer.

questions.text: why is checkout hitting inventory twice and who decided that?
questions.note: Architecture question during an incident. CAT-DEP-001 is a declared map, not a design rationale, and says so.
